# Getting Started with THE GATEHUB

Welcome to **THE GATEHUB** — your platform for structured learning, Learning Universes, certificates, and instructor-led courses.

To access your account:

1. Open THE GATEHUB in your browser.
2. Click **Login** in the top-right corner of the navigation bar.
3. Enter your registered **email address** and **password**.
4. Click **Sign In**.

**First time?** Click **Sign Up** on the landing page, choose Student or Instructor, complete registration, then log in.

**Forgot your password?** On the login page, click **Forgot Password**, enter your email, and follow the reset link sent to your inbox.

1. Visit the landing page and click **Sign Up**.
2. Choose **Student** or **Instructor** during registration.
3. Verify your email if prompted, then log in.

- Browse courses from **Dashboard → Browse**.
- Enroll in free courses instantly; paid courses use secure checkout.
- Open **Learning Universes** for track-based structured paths.
- Track progress, quizzes, projects, and certificates from your dashboard.

- Go to **Create Course** or **Create Learning Universe**.
- Use **Academic Authoring Studio** (LaTeX DSL) or **Visual Authoring Studio**.
- Publish content, set pricing, and review student project submissions.

- Access **Admin Dashboard** for users, courses, payments, and analytics.
- Configure platform settings, AI features, and certificates.

- [Student Manual](/help/student)
- [Instructor Manual](/help/instructor)
- [Admin Manual](/help/admin)
- [FAQ](/help/faq)
# Student Manual
THE GATEHUB provides courses, Learning Universes, interactive practice, quizzes, projects, and certificates. This manual covers everything you need as a student.

Your dashboard shows enrolled courses, Learning Universes, recent activity, and certificate progress. Use the sidebar to navigate:

- **My Courses** — traditional video + notes courses
- **Browse** — discover new content
- **Certificates** — earned and in-progress certificates
- **Quiz Results** — history of quiz attempts

1. Open a course from Browse or the landing page.
2. Click **Enroll** (free) or **Buy Now** (paid).
3. After payment, access opens immediately.

- Watch lecture videos in the course player.
- Read compiled notes (PDF) alongside videos.
- Complete section quizzes when available.
Learning Universes are structured paths: **Tracks → Modules → Lessons → Content Blocks**.

1. Open a Learning Universe from Browse or your enrollments.
2. Use the lesson sidebar to move between lessons.
3. Content blocks render in order: theory, videos, practice, quizzes, projects.
Progress is saved automatically: lessons completed, videos watched, practice passed, quizzes passed, projects submitted.

- YouTube and Vimeo embeds play in-page.
- Uploaded videos stream from THE GATEHUB CDN.
- Video watch progress counts toward lesson completion.

- Lecture notes may appear as PDF or rich content blocks.
- Use fullscreen on PDFs for better reading.

Practice blocks include a code editor (Monaco), **Run**, **Reset**, **Show Solution**, and **Show Hint**.

Supported languages include Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, SQL, Java, C, C++, C#, and Go.

Your output is compared to the expected output for pass/fail.

- Single choice, multiple choice, and other question types may appear.
- Submit answers to see explanations.
- Passing all quizzes may be required for certificates.
Assignments show due dates, points, and instructions. Submit through the assignment interface when available.

Open the project workspace from the lesson. Submit via:

- GitHub repository URL
- Google Colab notebook link
- ZIP upload
- PDF report
- Text submission

1. Click **Launch Notebook** if a Colab URL is provided.
2. Complete the notebook.
3. Submit your Colab link or upload the `.ipynb` file.

1. Create a repository per instructions.
2. Submit the repository URL in the project workspace.
3. Wait for instructor review.

Certificate rules vary per course. Common requirements:

- Complete all lessons
- Pass all quizzes
- Submit and pass all projects
- Achieve minimum score (e.g. 70%)
Go to **Certificates** in the sidebar. Click **Download PDF** on earned certificates.

THE GATEHUB tracks:

- Lesson completion
- Video watched percentage
- Practice block completion
- Quiz pass status
- Project submission and approval
- Final exam pass (if applicable)

Resume from your last lesson automatically.
Leave course reviews after enrollment. Ratings help other students and instructors.
See the [FAQ](/help/faq) for common student questions.

- Check your internet connection.
- Try another browser (Chrome recommended).
- For uploaded videos, ensure you are enrolled.

- Verify language selection matches your code.
- Check for syntax errors in the output panel.

- Confirm all completion rules are met.
- Contact your instructor if requirements are complete but certificate is missing.
# Instructor Manual

1. Go to **Create Course** from the instructor sidebar.
2. Enter title, description, category, and pricing.
3. Use **AI Course Authoring** (optional) to generate curriculum drafts.
4. Build curriculum: sections, lectures, videos, notes, quizzes.
Set price in course settings. Use **0** for free courses. Paid courses integrate with the platform payment gateway.

- Save curriculum drafts as you build.
- Publish the course when ready — it becomes visible in Browse (subject to admin approval if configured).
- Unpublish to hide from new enrollments.
The Academic Authoring Studio uses a **Learning Universe DSL** in LaTeX (`main.tex`).

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `\overviewmarkdown` | Lesson overview |
| `\theory` | Main topic with title and body |
| `\note`, `\tip`, `\warning` | Callout blocks |
| `\image` | Image with caption |
| `\video` | YouTube, Vimeo, or upload |
| `\practice` | Try It Yourself block |
| `\quiz` | MCQ quiz |
| `\project` | Project with instructions |
| `\colab`, `\github` | Colab/GitHub project URLs |
| `\discussion` | Discussion prompt |
| `\assignment` | Graded assignment |
| `\resource`, `\download` | External links and files |
| `\checkpoint` | Progress marker |
| `\certificatecriteria` | Certificate rule text |
| `\finalexam` | Final exam block |
Click **Publish** in Academic Studio. DSL is parsed into structured `contentBlocks` JSON and stored in the database.
Access via **Create Learning Universe → Visual Studio**.

1. Build hierarchy: Track → Module → Lesson.
2. Select a lesson to open the lesson builder.
3. Add content blocks via **Add Block**.

Add a **Quiz** block. Configure:

- Single / multiple choice, true/false, fill-in-blank
- Questions, options, correct answers, explanations, marks
Add **Project**, **Colab Project**, or **GitHub Project** blocks. Set instructions, rubric, max marks, and submission type.
Add a **Practice** block with starter code, expected output, solution, and hints.
Use the Image block — drag and drop or click to upload. Add caption and alt text.
Use **Video Upload** block for MP4, WEBM, MOV. Files are bundled on publish.
Add **YouTube Video** block and paste the URL.
Add **Colab Project** block with notebook URL and deliverables. Students launch and submit from the player.
Add **GitHub Project** with repository template URL. Students submit repo links for review.
View enrollment counts, progress, and engagement from **Analytics** in the instructor dashboard.
Configure certificate criteria using `\certificatecriteria` blocks or Visual Studio certificate rules. Students earn certificates when all rules pass.
Go to **Project Reviews** to grade submissions: approve, reject, assign marks, and leave feedback.
Visit [FAQ](/help/faq) for instructor-specific questions.
# Admin Manual
The Admin Dashboard provides oversight of users, content, payments, and system health.

- View all users, filter by role.
- Suspend or activate accounts.
- Reset passwords when needed.
Review instructor applications if approval workflow is enabled. Approve or reject with notes.

- Monitor transactions in **Payments**.
- View Razorpay/Stripe settlement status.
- Handle refund requests per platform policy.
Platform-wide metrics: enrollments, revenue, active users, course completions, Learning Universe adoption.

- Audit issued certificates.
- Regenerate or revoke if policy requires.
- Configure certificate templates in Settings.
Moderate course reviews. Remove spam or policy violations.
**Settings → System Health** shows database, storage, AI provider status, and queue health.

**Settings → AI** tab:

- Enable/disable AI course authoring, LU builder, tutor, quiz generator
- Select provider: OpenAI, Gemini, or hybrid
- Set model name override

- Enforce strong passwords and session policies.
- Review audit logs (super admin).
- Rotate API keys via environment variables, not the database.
Verify payment gateway keys in server environment. Check webhook endpoints.
Confirm `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY` is set. Enable feature toggles in AI settings.
Check disk space and `UPLOAD_DIR` permissions on the server.
# Frequently Asked Questions

chunks.section: How do I enroll in a course?
chunks.content: Open the course page and click **Enroll** or **Buy Now**. Paid courses require checkout completion.
Complete all required lessons, quizzes, and projects per the course rules. Certificates appear under **Certificates** when earned.

chunks.section: How do I submit a GitHub project?
chunks.content: Open the project lesson, click **Open Workspace**, paste your repository URL, and submit.

chunks.section: Can I resume where I left off?
chunks.content: Yes. Learning Universe progress saves automatically. Reopen the course to continue from your last lesson.

chunks.section: How do I create a quiz?
chunks.content: In Visual Studio, add a **Quiz** block. In Academic Studio, use `\quiz` with `\question` and `\option` commands.

chunks.section: How do I publish a Learning Universe?
chunks.content: Complete your content in Visual or Academic Studio, then click **Publish**. Assets upload with the publish request.
Both produce identical `contentBlocks` JSON. Academic uses LaTeX DSL; Visual uses a drag-and-drop builder.

chunks.section: How do I enable AI features?
chunks.content: Go to **Admin → Settings → AI** and toggle features. Ensure API keys are configured on the server.
Rules like "complete all lessons", "pass all quizzes", "minimum 70% score". Defined per course in authoring.
Instructors review submissions in **Project Reviews**, assign marks, and approve or reject.
The platform integrates with Razorpay/Stripe depending on deployment configuration.

chunks.section: Can I make a course free?
chunks.content: Set price to **0** in course or Learning Universe settings.
A structured learning path with tracks, modules, lessons, and ordered content blocks (theory, video, quiz, project, etc.).
# Troubleshooting

- Clear browser cache and cookies.
- Use **Forgot Password** to reset.
- Ensure you are on the correct role (student vs instructor URL).

- Disable ad blockers for embedded YouTube/Vimeo.
- For uploaded videos, confirm enrollment is active.

- Match the language selector to your code.
- Python and JavaScript run server-side; HTML/CSS may preview in-browser.

- **Colab URL invalid** — use a full `colab.research.google.com` notebook URL.
- **Asset not found** — upload images/videos before publishing in Visual Studio.

- If PDF fails to load, try downloading instead of inline view.
- Large PDFs may take time on slow connections.
Use the **THE GATEHUB Assistant** (bottom-right) for documentation-based answers.
# Release Notes

- Help Center at `/help` (public, no login required)
- Student, Instructor, and Admin manuals
- Full-text documentation search
- PDF export for manuals
- THE GATEHUB AI Assistant (documentation RAG)
- Context-aware help on key pages
- Onboarding tours for student, instructor, and admin

- Full lesson builder with 28 block types
- Asset upload on publish
- Split-screen student preview

- Academic Authoring Studio (LaTeX DSL)
- Student player with progress tracking
- Project submissions (GitHub, Colab, ZIP)
# Integrations Guide
THE GATEHUB connects with external tools so students and instructors can code, research, and collaborate without leaving the platform.
Coding Labs can launch **Google Colab** notebooks for hands-on Python exercises. Students run code in Colab and submit work back to THE GATEHUB.

chunks.section: Student: Open Colab from a lesson
chunks.content:
1. Enroll in the Learning Universe and open the lesson.
2. Navigate to the **Coding Lab** step.
3. Click **Open in Google Colab** (or **Connect Colab**).
4. Sign in with Google if prompted and authorize THE GATEHUB.
5. Complete the notebook and use **Submit** in the lesson when finished.

chunks.section: Instructor: Add Colab to a lesson
chunks.content:
1. Open **Visual Authoring Studio** or **Academic Studio**.
2. Add a **Coding Lab** component to the lesson.
3. Paste a valid Colab notebook URL or create a new notebook.
4. Publish the Learning Universe so students see the lab.

- **Colab won't open**: Check the notebook URL is public or shared correctly.
- **Authorization failed**: Reconnect Google from **Settings → Integrations**.
- **Submit not working**: Return to the lesson tab and click Submit after saving in Colab.
The **Research Workspace** lets students and instructors write LaTeX papers with **Overleaf** integration.

1. Open a lesson with a **Research Paper** or **Research Workspace** step.
2. Click **Open in Overleaf** or **Launch Overleaf**.
3. Edit your `.tex` project; changes sync back to THE GATEHUB workspace.
4. Compile PDF inside Overleaf or THE GATEHUB preview.
Instructors authoring in **Academic Authoring Studio** use LaTeX DSL commands. Compile from the studio toolbar. Errors appear in the compile log panel.
Connected Google accounts can import/export project files. Manage connections under **Settings → Integrations**.

| Role | Colab | Overleaf | Drive |
|------|-------|----------|-------|
| Student | Use in enrolled lessons | Use in research steps | Optional import |
| Instructor | Author labs | Author research steps | Import templates |
| Admin | Configure platform OAuth | Configure platform OAuth | Platform settings |

- Student Manual → Projects and Coding Labs
- Instructor Manual → Learning Universe authoring
- Troubleshooting → Code blocks and integrations
# Learning Universe Guide

A **Learning Universe** is THE GATEHUB's structured learning product: tracks, modules, lessons, quizzes, coding labs, research papers, and projects. It is different from a legacy **Course** (video + sections model).

| Feature | Learning Universe | Traditional Course |
|---------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Structure | Tracks → Modules → Lessons → Steps | Sections → Lectures |
| Authoring | Visual Studio or Academic Studio | Curriculum builder |
| Labs | Coding Lab, Notebook, Research | Optional resources |
| Progress | Per-step checkpoints | Lecture completion |

1. Browse or open a Learning Universe from **Dashboard → My Courses** or the public course page.
2. Click **Enroll** (free or paid).
3. Open **Continue Learning** to enter the player.
4. Use the **course outline** sidebar to switch lessons.
5. Complete steps: read content, take quizzes, open labs, submit projects.
6. Earn a **certificate** when all requirements are met.

1. Go to **Instructor Dashboard → Create Course** or **Learning Universe → New**.
2. Choose **Visual Authoring Studio** (block-based) or **Academic Authoring Studio** (LaTeX DSL).
3. Add tracks, modules, and lessons.
4. Add components: overview, objectives, quiz, coding lab, research paper, project.
5. **Preview** as a student from the instructor menu.
6. **Publish** when content and branding are complete.

- **Checkpoints** gate progression (quiz pass, lab submit, project approval).
- Students see **course progress** in the lesson header.
- Instructors review **project submissions** under **Project Reviews**.
Before publish, ensure: title, description, branding, at least one lesson, and pricing (if premium). Draft universes are visible only to instructors until published.

- Instructor list: `/instructor/courses`
- Visual studio: `/instructor/learning-universe/new/visual`
- Academic studio: `/instructor/learning-universe/new/academic`
- Student player: `/learning-universe/{id}/learn`
# Coding Lab Guide
**Coding Labs** are interactive programming steps inside a Learning Universe lesson. They support in-browser exercises and **Google Colab** notebooks.

1. Open the lesson from **My Courses → Continue Learning**.
2. Select the **Coding Lab** step in the lesson outline.
3. Read instructions in the workspace panel.
4. **Run code** in the embedded editor or click **Open in Google Colab**.
5. Click **Submit** when your solution passes tests (if autograding is enabled).
6. Use **Previous / Next** to move between lesson steps.
Some labs use THE GATEHUB's built-in code runner. Click **Run**, view output in the console panel, and fix errors shown in red.

1. Click **Connect Colab** or **Open in Google Colab**.
2. Authorize Google on first use (**Settings → Integrations**).
3. Complete the notebook; return to THE GATEHUB to submit.

- Check language matches the lab (usually Python).
- Ensure inputs are valid and required packages are allowed.

- Run all required cells in Colab.
- Pass hidden tests if the lab uses autograding.
- Confirm you are enrolled in the universe.
Coding Labs appear only on the lesson step labeled **Coding Lab**. Open the course outline and select that step.

1. Visual Studio → add **Coding Lab** block to a lesson.
2. Set starter code, instructions, and optional Colab URL.
3. Configure test cases if supported.
4. Preview and publish.

- Integrations Guide → Google Colab
- Student Manual → Quizzes and Projects
# Research Workspace Guide
The **Research Workspace** is for writing academic papers in LaTeX with optional **Overleaf** integration.

1. Enroll in a Learning Universe with a **Research Paper** step.
2. Navigate to that step in the lesson player.
3. The workspace opens with a LaTeX editor and PDF preview.

1. Edit `main.tex` or section files in the editor.
2. Click **Compile** to generate PDF.
3. Fix errors using the compile log (missing packages, undefined references).
4. Save frequently; versions may be stored in your project.

1. Click **Open in Overleaf** from the workspace toolbar.
2. Authorize Overleaf if prompted.
3. Edit in Overleaf; sync returns to THE GATEHUB project.
4. Submit the final PDF from the lesson **Submit** button if required.
Use `\cite{}` with a `.bib` file or `thebibliography` environment. Academic Studio lessons may include templates with preloaded bibliography styles.

1. Add a **Research Paper** component in Visual or Academic Studio.
2. Provide a template `.tex` starter.
3. Set submission requirements (PDF upload, word count, due date).
4. Grade submissions under **Project Reviews**.

- **Compile failed**: Read the log line number; common fixes are missing `\begin{document}`, unescaped `%`, or missing packages.
- **Overleaf won't connect**: Re-link from **Settings → Integrations**.
- **PDF blank**: Run compile twice for table of contents and references.

- Integrations Guide → Overleaf
- Instructor Manual → Academic Authoring Studio
# Publishing Guide
Publishing makes your **Course** or **Learning Universe** visible to students. Draft content stays private to instructors and admins.

1. **Title and description** filled in branding setup.
2. At least one **track** with a **lesson**.
3. All required steps have content (no empty quizzes or labs).
4. **Pricing** set (free or premium) if selling.
5. **Thumbnail / banner** uploaded (recommended).
6. Click **Publish** from the studio or course management page.

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| Missing title | Course branding setup |
| No lessons | Add content in Visual or Academic Studio |
| Validation errors | Open compile/preview panel and fix errors |
| Draft only | Click **Publish** not just Save |
| Permission denied | Confirm instructor role is approved |
| Payment not configured | Admin must enable payments for paid courses |

1. **Instructor → My Courses → Edit course**.
2. Complete curriculum (sections, lectures, videos).
3. Set price and category.
4. Submit for review if admin approval is required.
5. Status changes to **Published** when approved.

- Students find courses via **Browse**, category hubs, or direct links.
- Updates to content may require re-publish or save depending on the editor.
- Unpublish or archive from course settings (instructor/admin).
Published courses appear in search and browse. Unpublished drafts return 404 or "not available" for students.

- Learning Universe Guide
- Instructor Manual → Course creation
- Troubleshooting → Publish issues
# AI Assistant Guide

THE GATEHUB Assistant is the official intelligent guide for the entire platform. It answers questions about courses, Learning Universes, Academic Studio, coding labs, research papers, Colab, Overleaf, certificates, publishing, payments, and every dashboard.

You do not need to search documentation manually — ask in plain language.

- Click **Ask Assistant** (floating button on any page).
- In Help Center, click **AI** in the header or **Ask AI Assistant** in the table of contents.
- Press **Ctrl+/** (Windows) or **⌘/** (Mac) from anywhere on the site.

The assistant is synchronized with official documentation:

- Getting Started, Student, Instructor, and Admin manuals
- Product guides: Learning Universe, Coding Lab, Research Workspace, Integrations, Publishing
- FAQ, Troubleshooting, and Release Notes
- Platform navigation paths for one-click links in answers

It also uses your **current page** and **role** to tailor answers. On the Coding Lab, it prioritizes run/submit/Colab help. In the Instructor Dashboard, it prioritizes authoring and publishing.

- How do I create a Learning Universe?
- How do certificates work?
- Where is Google Colab?
- How do I publish my course?
- Why isn't my quiz submitting?
- What is a checkpoint?
- What is the difference between Learning Universe and Course?
- What is Academic Studio?

- **Streaming responses** — answers appear as they are generated.
- **Stop generating** — halt a long response mid-stream.
- **Regenerate** — get a fresh answer to your last question.
- **Copy** — copy any assistant message.
- **Clear chat** — reset the conversation.
- **Suggested follow-ups** — tap chips after each answer.
- **Sources** — jump to the exact documentation section cited.
- **History** — your last messages persist across page navigation (same browser).
When the assistant tells you where to go, it includes clickable links such as [Instructor Dashboard](/instructor) or [Certificates](/student/certificates). Click to navigate directly.

- Check your internet connection.
- Try again — the assistant falls back to documentation search if AI is temporarily unavailable.
- Use **Help Center → Search** (⌘K) as a backup.

- Rephrase with more context: "I'm on the quiz builder and save fails."
- Click **Regenerate** or ask a follow-up: "What are the required fields?"
- Open the **Sources** links for the full official section.
Conversations are processed to answer your question. Chat history is stored locally in your browser only (not synced across devices).
Platform admins configure the AI model in **Admin → Settings**. Documentation index is rebuilt when developers run `npm run docs:sync` in the backend after doc updates.
